blocks.arabic_text: قَالُوا: خَيْرُ إِخْوَانٍ، أَلَانُوْا فِرَاشَنأَ، وَاطَابُوا مَطْعَمَنَا، وَبَاتُوا وَأَصْبَحُوا يُعَلِّمُونَنَا كِتَابَ رَبِّنَا تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَي وَسُنَّةَ نَبِيِّنَاﷺ، فَأَعْجَبَتِ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ وَفَرِحَ بِهَا، ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْنَا رَجُلاً رَجُلاً، فَعَرَضْنَا عَلَيْهِ مَا تَعَلَّمْنَا وَعُلِّمْنَا، فَمِنَّا مَنْ عُلِّمََ التَّحِيَّاتِ وَأُمَّ الْكِتَابِ وَالسُّورَةَ وَالسُّورَتَيْنِ وَالسُّنَنَ.
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Shihab ibn Abbad (RH) narrates, “A delegation from the tribe of Abd al-Qais had gone to the presence of Rasulullah ﷺ. I heard one of the members of that delegation describing the details of their journey. He says: “When we went to the presence of Rasulullah ﷺ, the Muslims were overjoyed at our arrival. When we came to the gathering of the Prophet ﷺ, the people made room for us. We sat down there. Rasulullah ﷺ welcomed us and made du'a for us. Then, looking at us, he asked, “Who is your leader and the one responsible for you?” All of us pointed towards Mundhir ibn A'idh. Seeing him, the Prophet ﷺ asked, “Is this Ashajj — the one with the scar of a wound — your leader?” and we said, “Yes.” (When someone has scars of a wound on his head or face, he is called Ashajj.) There was the scar of a wound on his face because a donkey's hoof had struck it. That is why he got the name Ashajj, and it was on that day that this name was given to him for the first time. He had stayed behind his travelling companions; he tied up his companions' mounts and arranged their belongings properly.
